text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- International stock markets shaken by heavy falls in indices. German DAX index of 30 leading shares falls 3.9 percent to 3,295.93 points.
- Bosnian refugee children brought out of Sarajevo four and a half years ago taken back home, as federal states say they will stick to repatriation of thousands of refugees.

- Number of ethnic Germans from the former Soviet Union and eastern Europe moving to the country falls by 17 percent compared to same period last year as more fail the German language test required for entry.
- Employers association (CDA) of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats want lower salaries for poorly qualified long-term unemployed to boost their chances of employment.
- A Turkish man injured after a fire broke out at his home in the central German town of Haigerseelbach and investigators are not ruling out the possibility of a racist attack.
HANDELSBLATT
- Wall Street fall sends down markets worldwide, the dollar falling to 1.6664 marks.
- CDA says wants a society-wide contract for full employment, with employers, employees and unions working together to create jobs.

- Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber wants credit business of Landesanstalt fuer Aufbaufinazierung (LfA) to be significantly limited after controversy over huge credit line sought by media concern Kirch Group.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Orphans brought out of the beseiged city of Sarajevo four and a half years ago taken home.
- German shares fall sharply after losses on Wall Street.
- Bavarian premier Stoiber says LfA should concentrate on supporting medium-sized businesses and says future lines of credit should be limited to 50 million marks.
- Job creation law comes into effect meaning that unemployed people must take up worse-paid job offers more quickly or risk losing benefits.
- No clues as to the cause of arson attack which left three members of a Turkish family dead. Authorities offer 50,000 mark reward for information.
DIE WELT
- Fear of rising U.S. interest rates leads to falls on international markets.
- CDA says wage growth should be kept under the rate of inflation in the future.
- Top Kohl's aide Wolfgang Schaeuble says ruling coalition ready to continue talks with opposition Social Democrats (SPD) over planned tax reforms at any time.
- No clues yet into arson attack on Turkish family.
- Bosnian children sent back to Sarajevo after four and a half years in Germany.
